title: The Mesozoic Era
keyIdea: The Mesozoic Era, from about 252 to 66 million years ago, is the age of dinosaurs. It has three periods in order: the Triassic (252 to 201 million years ago), the Jurassic (201 to 145) and the Cretaceous (145 to 66). Different dinosaurs lived in different periods, not all at the same time: Coelophysis lived in the Triassic, Stegosaurus and Brachiosaurus in the Jurassic, and Tyrannosaurus rex and Triceratops at the end of the Cretaceous. Stegosaurus lived about 83 million years before T. rex, a bigger gap than the 66 million years between T. rex and us. No people lived in the Mesozoic.
familyTip: Make a time line along a hallway or a long strip of paper: one big step or 10 cm for every 10 million years. Mark today at one end, then 66, 145, 201 and 252 million years ago. Put a toy or a drawing of each dinosaur at its time and see how far apart Stegosaurus and T. rex really are.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: order the three periods, measure them on a scaled time line, place five dinosaurs, measure the T. rex gap, and judge who could meet.

kid: The time of the dinosaurs is called the Mesozoic Era. It began about 252 million years ago and ended 66 million years ago. That is a huge stretch of time, so it is split into three parts, called periods.

The periods go in this order: Triassic, Jurassic, Cretaceous. Say T, J, C to remember it. The first dinosaurs lived in the Triassic. They were small and fast. The Cretaceous was the last period and the longest one.

Dinosaurs did not all live at the same time. Stegosaurus lived in the Jurassic. T. rex lived at the very end of the Cretaceous. The time between them is longer than the time between T. rex and you! So they never met.
No people lived in the Mesozoic. The era ended when a huge rock from space hit Earth. Most dinosaurs died out. Birds are the dinosaurs that lived on.
adult: Ages 7 to 9. This supports the Key Stage 2 science topic on rocks and fossils and evolution in the National Curriculum in England (Years 3 and 6) and NGSS 3-LS4-1 (fossils as evidence of organisms and environments of long ago). Dates are rounded from the International Chronostratigraphic Chart (2023); dinosaur dates are from the Natural History Museum Dino Directory. Key words: era, period, Mesozoic, Triassic, Jurassic, Cretaceous, million years ago, time line, extinction, fossil.

The lab has five tasks on one time line drawn to scale, from 252 million years ago to today. Children put the periods in order, then measure them: about 51, 56 and 79 million years. They drag five dinosaurs into their periods. They tap marks to measure two gaps: about 83 million years from Stegosaurus to T. rex, and 67 from T. rex to today. Last, they judge five pairs, using whether the two time bars overlap.

Common mistakes. Children often think all dinosaurs lived together, so pictures that show Stegosaurus fighting T. rex feel right. Other slips: the Jurassic was the longest or the only dinosaur period, the order is Jurassic, Triassic, Cretaceous, people and dinosaurs lived together, and a dinosaur kind lasted the whole era. Be careful with big numbers: 66 million years is far longer than all of human history, so a scaled time line helps more than words.

practice.prompt: Which list is in order, from oldest to youngest?
practice.hint: Think T, J, C. Which period had the very first dinosaurs?
practice.explain: The Triassic came first, then the Jurassic, then the Cretaceous, which ended 66 million years ago.

practice.prompt: The Jurassic began about 201 million years ago and ended about 145 million years ago. A dinosaur lived {n} million years after the Jurassic began. How many million years ago was that?
practice.hint: Count forward in time means fewer years ago. Take {n} away from 201.
practice.explain: 201 − {n} = {=201-n}, so it lived about {=201-n} million years ago, still in the Jurassic.

choices: At the end of the Cretaceous
practice.hint: Where did you drop T. rex on the time line in the lab?
practice.explain: T. rex lived about 68 to 66 million years ago, right at the end of the Cretaceous, just before the asteroid hit.

practice.prompt: Stegosaurus lived about 150 million years ago. Another animal lived {n} million years ago. How many million years apart are they?
practice.hint: Find the gap between the two dates: take {n} away from 150.
practice.explain: 150 − {n} = {=150-n} million years apart. A bar that ends before the other starts means they never met.

practice.prompt: Could Stegosaurus and T. rex have met?
choices: No, they lived about 83 million years apart
Yes, they lived at the same time
Yes, but only in the Triassic
practice.hint: Look at the two gaps you measured in the lab.
practice.explain: Stegosaurus lived about 150 million years ago and T. rex about 67. The gap is about 83 million years, more than from T. rex to us.

pool.hint: Remember T, J, C. Which period held the very first, small dinosaurs?
pool.explain: The Triassic was first, from about 252 to 201 million years ago. The first dinosaurs lived in it.

pool.hint: Which coloured block on the time line was the widest?
pool.explain: The Cretaceous lasted about 79 million years, longer than the Jurassic (about 56) or the Triassic (about 51).

pool.prompt: In which period did Stegosaurus live?
pool.hint: Stegosaurus lived about 150 million years ago. Which period covers that?
pool.explain: The Jurassic ran from about 201 to 145 million years ago, so 150 million years ago is late in the Jurassic.

pool.prompt: Did people live at the same time as dinosaurs like T. rex?
choices: No, people came tens of millions of years later
Yes, but only at the end
pool.hint: Where was the 'today' mark on the time line?
pool.explain: The first people lived about 300,000 years ago. T. rex died out 66 million years ago, long before.

pool.prompt: How did the Mesozoic Era end?
choices: An asteroid hit Earth and most dinosaurs died out
pool.explain: About 66 million years ago a huge asteroid hit Earth. Most dinosaurs died out, and only the birds lived on.

pool.prompt: Triceratops and T. rex both lived about 68 to 66 million years ago. Could they have met?
choices: No, they lived in different periods
pool.hint: Do the two time bars overlap?
pool.explain: Both lived at the end of the Cretaceous, so their bars overlap. Fossils of both are found in the same rocks.

choices: An era made of three periods
A place where fossils are found
pool.hint: Think of the three coloured blocks together.
pool.explain: The Mesozoic is an era, a long stretch of time, made of the Triassic, the Jurassic and the Cretaceous.

pool.prompt: The Cretaceous began about 145 million years ago and ended 66 million years ago. A dinosaur lived {n} million years before the end. How many million years ago was that?
pool.hint: Before the end means longer ago. Add {n} to 66.
pool.explain: 66 + {n} = {=66+n}, so it lived about {=66+n} million years ago, inside the Cretaceous.

pool.prompt: A period began {a} million years ago and ended {b} million years ago. How many million years did it last?
pool.hint: Take the end date away from the start date: {a} − {b}.
pool.explain: {a} − {b} = {=a-b} million years. Bigger numbers mean longer ago.
